content: The references and content provided are highly detailed and technical, reflecting a comprehensive collection of studies, guidelines, and expert contributions related to maternal and newborn health, particularly focusing on postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) prevention and management. 1. A statement by WHO, UNFPA, UNICEF, ICM, ICN, FIGO, and IPA emphasizes the importance of competent maternal and newborn health professionals. This document was accessed on December 6, 2018. 2. A cross-sectional study by Souza JP et al., published in The Lancet in 2013, explores interventions beyond essential measures to reduce maternal mortality. This study is part of the WHO Multicountry Survey on Maternal and Newborn Health. 3. Carroli G et al. conducted a systematic review on the epidemiology of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), published in Best Practice & Research Clinical Obstetrics & Gynaecology in 2008. The review highlights the prevalence, risk factors, and outcomes associated with PPH. 4. Oyelese Y and Ananth CV reviewed the epidemiology, risk factors, and causes of postpartum hemorrhage in Clinical Obstetrics and Gynecology in 2010, providing a detailed analysis of this critical maternal health issue. 5. Daru J et al. performed a multilevel analysis on the risk of maternal mortality in women with severe anemia during pregnancy and postpartum. This study, published in The Lancet Global Health in 2018, underscores the significant impact of anemia on maternal outcomes. 6. The WHO Executive Guideline Steering Group updated maternal and perinatal health recommendations between 2017 and 2019. These updates were accessed on December 5, 2018. 7. The WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd edition) provides a framework for creating evidence-based health guidelines. This document was accessed on December 6, 2018. 8. WHO recommendations for the prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage were published in 2018, offering evidence-based strategies to address this major cause of maternal mortality. 9. Wishart DS et al. updated the DrugBank database in 2018, providing a comprehensive resource for drug-related information, including medications relevant to maternal health. 10. Kim S et al. described the PubChem Substance and Compound databases in Nucleic Acids Research in 2016, which serve as valuable tools for understanding pharmacological agents used in obstetrics. 11. Alliance Pharmaceuticals provided information on Syntometrine ampoules, a uterotonic agent used in PPH prevention, through the electronic Medicines Compendium (eMC) website, accessed on November 9, 2018. 12. The International Pharmacopoeia (7th edition) by WHO, published in 2017, includes monographs on essential medicines like oxytocin and ergometrine for PPH prevention. 13. The WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (20th edition, amended August 2017) highlights key medications for maternal health, including uterotonic agents. 14. Gallos ID et al. conducted a network meta-analysis on uterotonic agents for PPH prevention, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2018. 15. Balshem H et al. outlined the GRADE guidelines for rating the quality of evidence in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2011, which are critical for developing maternal health recommendations. 16. Finlayson K et al. conducted a qualitative systematic review on the perspectives of women and healthcare providers regarding PPH prevention interventions. This review remains unpublished as of 2018. 17. Lawrie TA et al. reviewed the cost-effectiveness of uterotonic agents for PPH prevention in 2018, providing insights into economic considerations for maternal health interventions. 18. Meher S et al. developed core outcome sets for PPH prevention and treatment through an international Delphi consensus study, published in BJOG in 2018. 19. Widmer M et al. compared heat-stable carbetocin and oxytocin for PPH prevention after vaginal birth in a study published in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2018. 20. Oladapo OT et al. reviewed the efficacy of intramuscular versus intravenous prophylactic oxytocin for the third stage of labor in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2012. 21. Tunçalp Ö et al. evaluated the use of prostaglandins for PPH prevention in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2012. 22. Westhoff G et al. reviewed prophylactic oxytocin use during the third stage of labor to prevent PPH in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2013. 23. Liabsuetrakul T et al. assessed the prophylactic use of ergot alkaloids in the third stage of labor in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2018. 24. Su LL et al. reviewed carbetocin for PPH prevention in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2012. 25. Pantoja T et al. examined the use of oxytocin for PPH prevention in non-facility birth settings in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2016. 26. Finlayson K et al. explored the views and experiences of women and healthcare providers on PPH prevention and treatment interventions in a systematic review protocol registered in PROSPERO in 2018. 27. Downe S et al. conducted a systematic qualitative review on what matters to women during childbirth, published in PLOS One in 2018. 28. Higgins JPT and Green S edited the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, updated in March 2011. 29. Walsh D and Downe S appraised the quality of qualitative research in Midwifery in 2006, providing a framework for evaluating maternal health studies. 30. Evers S et al. developed a criteria list for assessing the methodological quality of economic evaluations in International Journal of Technology Assessment in Health Care in 2005. 31. Puhan MA et al. described the GRADE approach for rating the quality of treatment effect estimates from network meta-analyses in BMJ in 2014. 32. Brignardello-Petersen R et al. discussed advances in the GRADE approach for network meta-analyses in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2018. 33. Lewin S et al. introduced the GRADE-CERQual approach for qualitative evidence synthesis findings in Implementation Science in 2018. 34. Alonso-Coello P et al. presented the GRADE Evidence to Decision (EtD) frameworks for making informed healthcare choices in BMJ in 2016. 35. WHO published a report on inequalities in reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health, accessed on November 5, 2018. 36. WHO outlined standards for improving the quality of maternal and newborn care in health facilities, accessed on December 6, 2018. 37. WHO monographs on oxytocin injection and ergometrine hydrogen maleate provide detailed information on these uterotonic agents in the International Pharmacopoeia (7th edition). 38. WHO recommendations on optimizing health worker roles to improve access to maternal and newborn health interventions through task shifting were accessed on November 6, 2018. 39. A survey on the quality of medicines identified by the United Nations Commission on Life-Saving Commodities for Women and Children was conducted in 2015. 40. WHO evaluated the quality of care for severe pregnancy complications using the near-miss approach for maternal health, accessed on December 6, 2018.
